text:
sam: Heads up — main CI turned red after the poetry lock regen PR merged.
sam: ~30 integration runs failing, looks concentrated on int/redis-conn and int/worker-redis.
sam: Example error from the job logs:
```
requests.exceptions.SSLError: [SSL: TLSV1_ALERT_PROTOCOL_VERSION] tlsv1 alert protocol version (_ssl.c:XXXX)
  File "/workspace/.venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/httpx/_client.py", line 210, in send
    raise SSLError(e)
...
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
ssl.SSLError: SSL handshake failed
```
sam: Can someone help triage? suspect something pulled a newer cryptography/pyOpenSSL or changed TLS defaults.

maria: I saw this in the failed CI matrix earlier. The lock regen bumped cryptography from 41.x -> 42.x in the transitive tree.
maria: It also pulled in a newer certifi; could be CA chain ordering, but the TLS alert points to protocol version not certs.

jake: @ci-bot can you re-run the failing int/redis-conn job for commit abc1234 so we have a fresh log? I want to confirm reproducibility.

ci-bot: Rerun triggered for job int/redis-conn at commit abc1234. Queue position: 2. ETA ~3m.

anya: I pulled the lockfile locally and installed into a clean ubuntu:20 image — I can reproduce the handshake immediately in the same test.
anya: On the build image, openssl version is 1.1.1f. Newer cryptography may be trying to negotiate TLS1.3 and hitting an incompatibility with our alpine/musl builder binary wheel.

ken: Could also be manylinux wheel or wheel tag change causing different OpenSSL bindings. Did the lock regen also change the binary wheel resolution (cp310-cp310 vs cp310-manylinux_2014)?

jake: Starting a quick bisect across the set of lockfile updates. Running:
```
./scripts/lock-bisect --target=int/redis-conn --since=2026-03-14 --until=2026-03-18
```
jake: Will post the commit that flips the failure.

maria: FYI we reverted the lock regen in a revert PR (#4931) as an emergency mitigation — that unblocks a few downstream pipelines but main still shows the failing job (maybe cached runners picked up the new image).

ci-bot: Rerun finished for int/redis-conn (abc1234) — result: failure. Same SSLError shown in the log.

sam: If bisect points to cryptography/pyOpenSSL, we can test forcing cryptography==41.3 on CI image as a short-term workaround. Long term we should upgrade build images (openssl) or use manylinux wheels that are compatible.

anya: Agree. I can spin a small image with openssl 3.x and test installing the new lock to see if that fixes the handshake.

jake: Bisect step 3 -> failure flipped between lock snapshot 2026-03-16 and 2026-03-17. Narrowing now. If it lands on a transitive pin I'll open a minimal pin PR.

maria: Also adding logs to the bisect run: capturing pip resolver output and wheel tags. Might give a hint about which wheel changed.

sam: Thanks all. @jake please ping me when you open the pin PR so we can get a quick revert merged if needed. If anyone is oncall and wants to take the bisect over, go ahead.

ken: Noted — I'll watch the bisect output and help validate any workaround PRs.

jake: Opening a WIP PR to force cryptography==41.3 and rerun the matrix if bisect confirms. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4940 (WIP)

sam: :thumbsup:, let's keep communications here. If we confirm the root cause we can update the release notes / postmortem for lock regeneration process.
